newsitem.title: USA: Nasal strip maker sees product to suppress the appetite.
newsitem.headline: Nasal strip maker sees product to suppress the appetite.

text.p: The maker of an adhesive strip used to treat snoring said Thursday it hopes to offer by early next year a product to suppress the appetite or to quit smoking.

Minneapolis-based CNS Inc. has been developing a product, delivered by inhaling, which has shown on a preliminary basis to suppress appetite and act as an aid in curbing the desire to smoke, CNS President Richard Jahnke told a Piper Jaffray investment conference here.
The active ingredient is a food additive and Jahnke said the Food and Drug Administration requested safety data on it.
But before the company funded extensive research to provide the data, it decided to package the active ingredient in a lozenge form and a gum form to test the effectiveness of the product.

The first trials are expected to be conducted this summer with some results available in early fall. "We will hopefully take the product to market, perhaps with reduced claims, as early as next year," Jahnke said.

CNS' major product is Breathe Right, a nonprescription, small adhesive strip which, when placed across the bridge of the nose, opens nasal passages and improves breathing. The device is marketed to treat snoring and congestion caused by colds and allergies.
CNS's stock rose 18.75 cents to $9.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
